1.visual: Two interlocking chain links arranged diagonally, forming the classic hyperlink symbol. The links are rendered as thick rounded rectangles overlapping at the center.
1.usage: Copy or share a URL, insert a hyperlink in a text editor, link two related records, display a connected/linked state.

2.visual: A checklist with two rows, each showing a bold checkmark on the left and a short horizontal line representing text on the right. The checkmarks are large and the lines are medium-length.
2.usage: View a to-do list, display task completion status, show a checklist form, represent a list of verified items.

3.visual: Two diagonal arrows pointing away from each other — one toward the upper-right and one toward the lower-left — connected by a dashed line in the middle, indicating expansion or fullscreen.
3.usage: Expand a panel to fullscreen, maximize a modal or card, scale content outward, enter an expanded view mode.

4.visual: A single upward-pointing arrow whose shaft splits into two branches diverging to the lower-left and lower-right, resembling a merge or fork shape pointing upward.
4.usage: Merge two branches into one, combine multiple inputs into a single output, represent a git merge action, indicate consolidation.

5.visual: Two diagonal arrows pointing toward each other — one from the upper-right and one from the lower-left — both aimed at the center, indicating compression or collapse.
5.usage: Collapse a fullscreen view, minimize or compress a panel, shrink content to fit, exit an expanded view mode.

6.visual: A single short, thick horizontal line centered in the icon with rounded ends, representing a minus or remove symbol.
6.usage: Remove an item from a list, decrease a quantity, collapse a section, indicate a subtraction or deletion action.

7.visual: A cursor arrow pointer angled to the lower-left with short radiating lines around its tip, suggesting a click or tap action with visual feedback.
7.usage: Indicate a clickable element, represent an interactive cursor, show click or tap feedback, highlight a selectable area.

8.visual: Four arrows pointing outward in all four cardinal directions (up, down, left, right) from a shared center point, forming a cross or move symbol.
8.usage: Drag and reposition an element, move a widget on a canvas, indicate a draggable item, represent pan or move mode.

9.visual: A paperclip shape with a looping oval form tapering to a point at the bottom, rendered in the classic diagonal paperclip orientation.
9.usage: Attach a file to a message or form, indicate an attachment is present, add a document to an email, link a file resource.

10.visual: A pencil or pen shape oriented diagonally from lower-left to upper-right, with a pointed tip at the lower-left and a flat eraser end at the upper-right.
10.usage: Edit or modify content, open a text or field editor, rename an item, annotate a document.

11.visual: A pushpin with a round head at the top and a narrow vertical stem pointing downward, viewed from the front with the pin centered and symmetric.
11.usage: Pin an item to stay visible, mark a pinned or saved message, indicate a fixed/sticky element, add a location marker.

12.visual: A pushpin shape with a diagonal line crossing through it from upper-left to lower-right, indicating a disabled or negated pin state.
12.usage: Unpin an item, remove a pinned status, indicate unpinning is available, show a not-pinned state.

13.visual: A large plus sign with four equal arms of uniform thickness, centered in the icon, representing add or create.
13.usage: Add a new item or record, create a new entry, expand a collapsed section, insert content into a list or canvas.

14.visual: A curved arrow that arcs to the left and then turns sharply to point right, resembling a forward-redirect or redo shape with the arrowhead on the right side.
14.usage: Redo an undone action, forward a message, redirect to another destination, indicate a reply-forward gesture.

15.visual: Two circular arrows forming a complete refresh loop — one arc on the upper-left curving clockwise and one on the lower-right, with arrowheads at both tips pointing in opposite directions.
15.usage: Refresh or reload data, sync content between two sources, retry a failed operation, indicate a two-way sync process.

16.visual: A small square in the lower-left with a downward-pointing arrow above it and a dotted/dashed partial square shape in the upper-right, suggesting an item being dragged or dropped into place.
16.usage: Drag and drop an element, move a component to a target zone, indicate a drop target, represent a reorder action.

17.visual: A rocket ship silhouette pointing toward the upper-right, with a rounded body, a pointed nose cone, and a small flame or exhaust detail at the lower-left tail.
17.usage: Launch a new project or app, indicate a deploy or publish action, represent speed or acceleration, show a startup or onboarding action.

18.visual: A circular arrow forming almost a full circle with the arrowhead on the left side pointing counterclockwise, representing undo or rotate-left.
18.usage: Undo the last action, rotate content counterclockwise, go back to a previous state, replay from the beginning.

19.visual: A circular arrow forming almost a full circle with the arrowhead on the right side pointing clockwise, representing redo or rotate-right.
19.usage: Redo a previously undone action, rotate content clockwise, advance to the next state, refresh in a forward direction.

20.visual: A floppy disk shape with a square body, a rectangular cutout at the top-right corner for the label area, and a smaller rectangle centered at the bottom representing the disk slot.
20.usage: Save a file or document, trigger a save action in an editor, indicate unsaved changes, store current work.

21.visual: Four right-angle corner brackets at each of the four corners of an imaginary rectangle, with open space in the center, representing a fullscreen or focus frame.
21.usage: Enter fullscreen mode, focus on a selected area, frame or crop content, indicate a scan or capture region.

22.visual: A pair of scissors with two circular handle loops on the left and two open blades extending to the upper-right and lower-right, in the classic cut symbol orientation.
22.usage: Cut selected text or content, remove a clipping from a layout, trigger a cut action in an editor, separate a portion of content.

23.visual: A magnifying glass with a circular lens on the upper-left and a short handle extending to the lower-right, representing search or zoom.
23.usage: Open a search field, zoom into content, find items in a list or page, trigger a search or filter action.

24.visual: An upward-pointing arrow emerging from a tray or box shape at the bottom — the box has an open top and the arrow points straight up out of it, representing an upload or share-from action.
24.usage: Upload a file, share content to an external destination, export data, send from a local device to a remote service.

25.visual: A single vertical arrow pointing downward that splits into two branches diverging upward-left and upward-right, resembling an upside-down fork or a split/branch shape.
25.usage: Fork a workflow into multiple paths, split a single input into two outputs, represent a branching decision, indicate a diverging process.

26.visual: A hand with the thumb pointing downward and fingers curled, the classic thumbs-down or dislike gesture, viewed at a slight angle.
26.usage: Dislike or downvote content, rate something negatively, reject a suggestion, indicate disapproval in a feedback system.

27.visual: A hand with the thumb pointing upward and fingers curled forward, the classic thumbs-up or like gesture, viewed at a slight angle.
27.usage: Like or upvote content, approve a suggestion, give positive feedback, indicate agreement or endorsement.

28.visual: A trash can with a rectangular body, a flat lid at the top with a small handle tab, and two vertical lines inside the body representing slots or dividers.
28.usage: Delete an item or file, move content to the trash, permanently remove a record, clear selected items.

29.visual: A curved arrow that arcs upward to the right and then turns to point back to the left, resembling a reply or undo shape with the arrowhead on the left side.
29.usage: Reply to a message, undo the last action, go back to a previous step, return to a prior state.

30.visual: Two curved arc segments breaking apart from each other — one in the upper-right and one in the lower-left — with small radiating tick marks at the break points, suggesting a chain or link being severed.
30.usage: Unlink or disconnect two items, remove a hyperlink, break a connection between records, indicate a broken or invalid link.
